case_name: THEIA Firefox Drakon APT BinFmt-Elevate Inject
ground_truth_summary: A Firefox visit to www.nhra.com established a Drakon backdoor. The operator used the BinFmt-Elevate capability, enumerated processes, injected into sshd, and the injected shellcode wrote sshdlog to disk.

attack_stages.summary: Firefox browsed to www.nhra.com and a Drakon backdoor console connected to the target.
The report identifies C2 connections to 189.141.204.211:80 and 208.203.20.42:80.
The BinFmt-Elevate capability ultimately changed the console identity to uid 0 root.
The operator enumerated processes and selected the sshd process (PID 1162 in the report).
The operator injected shellcode into sshd using Inject2.

data_quality_notes: The operational log records THEIA publishing and recording instability before 14:30 EDT on 2019-05-15; the selected attack begins at 14:48 EDT after publishing resumed.
The report says the hosts that were not publishing eventually pushed out accumulated data; event-level completeness is therefore an extraction-time validation question, not an assumption.
No event UUID, database table, timestamp field, or motif is asserted until the PGDMP archive is cataloged and extracted.

trace_confirmed_observables: Two /sbin/modprobe -q -- binfmt-0000 executions at 14:50 and 14:54 EDT
The /var/log/sshdlog artifact opened by /usr/sbin/sshd at 14:58 EDT
Benign load_helper.ko and read_scan.ko driver installations

notes: This case was selected only after M3a, its STOP semantics, and channel priors were frozen. It is a true cross-engagement holdout, not an input to method design or parameter tuning. The ground truth supports campaign-level reconstruction, not attribution to a named threat actor.
